20th People's Majlis

People's Majlis

People's Majlis Committee Minutes

17th Meeting of the General Committee

20 October 2026

Venue: People's Majlis building (Committee Room 6)

Start time: 11:41

{Chaired by the Committee Chair; Member for Hulhudhoo constituency Mohamed Shahid}

Remarks from the Chair:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I welcome all honourable members to the 17th meeting of the General Committee. What we are proceeding with on the committee's agenda today is the amendment submitted to Article 191 of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, which the Secretariat of the People's Majlis has sent to this committee to study and decide on. As you will know, an honourable member of the People's Majlis earlier submitted this to the Majlis Secretariat in order to bring an amendment to it. So, on that basis, the Secretariat has sent the matter to the committee together with having it placed on today's agenda. So, before we proceed, I will read out the committee's attendance. Abdul Sattar Mohamed, Holhudhoo constituency; Ahmed Riyaz, Thimarafushi constituency; Ibrahim Didi, Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency; Hussain Riza Adam, Maafushi constituency; Mohamed Ali, Dhuvaafaru constituency; Ameen Faisal, Kanditheemu constituency; Hussain Imran Latheef, Henveyru Dhekunu constituency; and myself, Mohamed Shahid, Hulhudhoo constituency. So, in accordance with Article 270(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, the matter submitted to amend Article 191 of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis is: To bring the following amendment to the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis. 1- To amend Article 191 of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis as follows. What you see on the TV screen now is the amendment that has come to us. I will ask the administrative desk to read out this amendment.

Remarks from the administrative desk:

Thank you, honourable Chair. The amendment submitted to the People's Majlis, submitted to Article 191. 1- To amend Article 191 of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis as follows. 191- Difference between a resolution and a bill. Any member of the Majlis may submit a resolution. Compared with a bill, a resolution has the following differences. That is: (a)- A resolution, unlike a bill, contains a preamble. (b)- That it is not a resolution on a subject related to the debate that will take place on a resolution already submitted. (c)- A resolution shall be put to a vote for acceptance before the preliminary debate on the resolution begins; if it is

[stamp]

passed that the resolution be accepted, after the preliminary debate the resolution shall then proceed to the committee related to that resolution. If it is not passed that the resolution be accepted, that resolution is void. There shall be no further debate on that resolution. (d)- That once the committee stage is completed and the resolution is passed by the Majlis, it need not be sent for ratification in the manner in which a bill is sent for ratification. 2- This amendment shall come into force from the date on which the People's Majlis passes this amendment. Thank you.

Remarks from the Chair:

Yes! So, I will open the floor to all honourable members. I give the floor to the honourable Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency, Ibrahim Didi.

Remarks by the Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency, Ibrahim Didi:

Thank you, honourable Chair. In accordance with Article 272(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, the amendment to Article 90, to Article 91 of the People's Majlis Rules, has been submitted by Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru, of Thulhaadhoo constituency. There is no great difference in this. I think the honourable member submitted this amendment with the intention of setting it out in a little more detail. So, I will read out what this amendment says. To amend Article 91 of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis as follows. Any member of the Majlis may submit a resolution. Compared with a bill, a resolution has the following differences. (a)- That a resolution, unlike a bill, contains a preamble. So, looking at it this way, this amendment comes to (b) and (c) of this. When it comes, (b) of this says: that it is not a resolution on the subject of a resolution previously submitted to the Majlis and proceeding. Not being a resolution that is on that subject. Then (c) of this says that the resolution must be put to a vote for acceptance before the preliminary debate on the resolution begins. Accordingly, if it is passed that the resolution be accepted, after the preliminary debate the resolution shall then proceed to a committee related to that resolution. So, I believe this is a very good amendment. And if it is passed that the resolution be accepted, to that resolution; if it is not passed, the resolution becomes void and on that resolution further

[stamp]

debate. So, this is what this amendment is. So, to pass this amendment in this way, and in addition there is a (d) in it. Once the committee stage is completed and the resolution is passed by the Majlis, it need not be sent for ratification in the manner in which a bill is sent for ratification. That is the difference between a resolution and a bill. That is already stated in Article 91 of the Majlis, in the Rules even now. That is, if it is a resolution it need not be sent for ratification. But if it is a bill it must be sent for ratification. So, I believe this is a very good amendment. Even now, without this amendment, resolutions are going in very much this kind of way. However, it has now been amended in a little more detail so that there is less room to create further problems with it. So, I propose that this be passed in this way. It would be good for me if some honourable member would second it.

Remarks from the Chair:

Yes! I will give the floor to Abdul Sattar Mohamed, Holhudhoo constituency.

Remarks by the Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed:

Yes! Thank you, Chair. I would like to say that I second the proposal just made by the honourable Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency, Ibrahim Didi.

Remarks from the Chair:

Yes! I give the floor to Ameen Faisal, Kanditheemu constituency.

Remarks by the Member for Kanditheemu constituency, Ameen Faisal:

Thank you, Chair. What I noted from this amendment is that, in reality, a resolution submitted under this and an urgent matter go along almost the same lines. An urgent matter, too, can be debated only after it is accepted. So, resolutions are also changing in that way. Members will be able to debate a resolution, too, only from the point this rule is passed. This rule will be passed. I have no doubt about that. That is, the PNC

[stamp]

majority is proceeding on the basis that it supports this proposal as it stands. So, this rule will be passed. So, after this rule is passed, in the People's Majlis there will be no opportunity to debate either an urgent matter or a resolution unless it has been accepted. But under this rule as it stands now, we, especially the minority, get the opportunity, even if an urgent matter is not accepted, to submit it as a resolution and debate on the floor of the Majlis whatever we see fit on it. So, this is not something I can support in any way. I believe there must be an opportunity in the People's Majlis for us, too, to say some word. Now, then, there will be none in an urgent matter, and none in a resolution either. So, this is not an amendment I can accept, which Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru, Thulhaadhoo constituency, has submitted. But I also accept that today's Majlis will run in accordance with the majority the people gave. So, we know this; even before, we had been expecting long ago that this amendment would come. So, I do not want to have any participation of mine where this is being passed. So, very best wishes and regards. So, I am leaving the committee.

Remarks from the Chair:

Yes! Thank you very much. What the honourable Member for Kanditheemu constituency, Ameen Faisal, just put forward was not a proposal. It was his concern or his view. So, there is no further proposal from any other member. It has been proposed by the honourable Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency, Ibrahim Didi, and seconded by the honourable Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed. That is, to bring the amendment being brought to Article 191(b) and (c) of these Rules. So, no other member has any further view. And since there is no wish to carry on any further debate on this matter, I will call a vote in the way it was just proposed and seconded. I ask the honourable members to vote as they see fit on bringing the amendment being brought to Article 191(b) and (c). (Voting) Thank you very much.

[stamp]

I announce that, by consensus of the committee, the amendment brought to Article 191(b) and (c), as proposed by the honourable Member for Feydhoo Dhekunu constituency, Ibrahim Didi, and seconded by the honourable Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed, has been passed. There is no further work on the agenda today. Therefore, I will conclude the committee at this point. I thank all honourable members very much for attending. Thank you.

[stamp]
